summary: The Health Care Freedom for Patients Act of 2025 makes several changes to health insurance exchanges, health savings accounts, Medicaid, and the Children's Health Insurance Program. It provides federal funding to make annual deposits into health savings accounts for certain individuals enrolled in bronze or catastrophic health plans during 2026 and 2027, funds cost-sharing reductions for silver plans beginning in 2027, and expands catastrophic plan eligibility to all individuals. Additionally, the bill alters federal matching rates for state Medicaid expansion programs based on whether states provide certain benefits to noncitizens, restricts Medicaid and CHIP coverage during citizenship or immigration verification periods, and prohibits federal funding and essential health benefit coverage for specific gender-transition procedures.

affected_groups.group: Individuals aged 18 to 64 with incomes up to 700% of the federal poverty level enrolled in bronze or catastrophic health

affected_groups.effect: Granted the option to purchase lower-premium catastrophic health plans beginning in 2027.

affected_groups.group: Medicaid, CHIP, and exchange plan enrollees seeking gender-transition procedures

key_provisions: Appropriates $10 billion for each of fiscal years 2026 and 2027 for the Department of Health and Human Services to deposit annual payments of $1,000 or $1,500 into health savings accounts for eligible enrollees aged 18 to 64 with household incomes up to 700% of the federal poverty level who are enrolled in bronze or catastrophic exchange plans.

Appropriates funds for cost-sharing reduction payments for individuals with silver plans and incomes up to 250% of the federal poverty level, starting in 2027, with exceptions for plans covering abortions.
Permits any individual purchasing health insurance in the individual market to enroll in a catastrophic plan starting in 2027, removing prior age and exemption limits.

Reduces the federal matching rate to 80% for the Medicaid expansion population in specified states that provide state-funded financial assistance or comprehensive health benefits to noncitizens who are not qualified aliens.

Prohibits federal Medicaid and CHIP payments for individuals whose citizenship, nationality, or satisfactory immigration status has not been verified by the end of standard verification periods, making state coverage during those periods optional.
Prohibits exchange plans from covering gender-transition procedures as an essential health benefit and bars federal Medicaid and CHIP funding for these procedures starting in 2027.

summary_detail.plain_summary: The Health Care Freedom for Patients Act of 2025 makes several changes to health insurance exchanges, health savings accounts, Medicaid, and the Children's Health Insurance Program. It provides federal funding to make annual deposits into health savings accounts for certain individuals enrolled in bronze or catastrophic health plans during 2026 and 2027, funds cost-sharing reductions for silver plans beginning in 2027, and expands catastrophic plan eligibility to all individuals. Additionally, the bill alters federal matching rates for state Medicaid expansion programs based on whether states provide certain benefits to noncitizens, restricts Medicaid and CHIP coverage during citizenship or immigration verification periods, and prohibits federal funding and essential health benefit coverage for specific gender-transition procedures.
summary_detail.significance: The bill proposes major financial incentives and policy shifts within federal health programs, modifying individual health insurance markets, health savings accounts, and federal contributions to state Medicaid and CHIP programs. Because it touches on marketplace subsidies, immigration-related Medicaid rules, and coverage restrictions for specific procedures, its provisions would alter federal health spending and insurance regulations for millions of participants and state agencies. The score for this dimension is assessed as 75 because it introduces wide-ranging structural modifications across multiple federal-state health programs.
